artists.biography: London producer Rob McAndrews who goes by the name Airhead and his spacious, abstract compositions are reminiscent of James Blake’s early work, and the comparison runs more than skin-deep: before the former even released a single solo track to his name, the pair put out a solid 10” single “Pembroke” in 2010 on Brainmath. Airhead has largely flown under the radar since. He followed up with the gorgeous “Paper Street” later that year, backed with an equally lovely Nick Höppner version. Signing to R&S Records seems to be one of the main affirmations of a breakthrough producer these days, and so it was no great surprise when it was announced earlier this year that he would release “Wait / South Congress” as a 10” single through the label, with a debut album to follow later in 2012.

perplexity.description:
Boing!! is the only full-length album by the British band Airhead, released in January 1992 on the Korova label. The album blends elements of electronic music and rock, characterized by melodic guitar work combined with synth textures, reflecting the early 1990s alternative and indie scene. Tracks like "Funny How" and "Counting Sheep" showcase the band's catchy, radio-friendly style with a mix of upbeat rhythms and introspective lyrics.

In the context of Airhead's discography, Boing!! stands as their sole album release, following several singles issued under the name Jefferson Airhead before a forced name change. The album reached number 29 on the UK charts, marking a modest commercial success. Despite this, the band was dropped by Korova shortly after, and their subsequent releases were limited to singles and an EP. Critically, Boing!! received moderate attention, with "Funny How" gaining notable airplay on BBC Radio 1 and even being used as intro music on the BBC football show Match of the Day, helping cement the band's brief presence in the early '90s British alternative rock landscape.
